headline.note: set explicitly in every fresh worker before native initialization on both runtimes

controlled_generation.prefill: single full-prompt forward, last-position-only output projection, no chunking, no next-token lookahead, no periodic cache clearing (both adapters)
controlled_generation.cache: full retention, per-request cache, no prefix reuse; KV dtype follows the case stored dtype (F32 for all three text cases)
controlled_generation.wired_limit: not set (neither runtime calls a setter)

stock_generation.prefill: installed generate_step split prefill (default chunk 2048): all-but-last prompt token as cache-only forwards, then one step on the last token; retains n+1 lookahead pipeline and cache clearing after every prefill chunk and n % 256 == 0
stock_generation.cache: shipped mlx_lm cache with its stock clearing policy; wired_limit context entered per the shipped stream_generate
stock_generation.wired_limit: stock shipped context (recommended working set 120259084288 B on this host)
stock_generation.note: stock adapters may stop early on the per-case stop set; actual emitted counts and finish reasons are recorded. Stock and controlled results are never pooled.

prompt_generator.seed_formula: case_initial_state = the z output of one splitmix64 step from state 0x20261105 ^ (index * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15)
prompt_generator.rule: token = z % vocab_size; advance state and retry while the token is in the case excluded stop set; per_length arrays are nested prefixes 32 | 512 | 2048 of the 2048 stream; the fixed-continuation workload uses prefix512[32:64]
prompt_generator.canonical_sha256: SHA-256 over the UTF-8 encoding of the JSON array of the token list with compact separators ',' and ':'

text_cases.name: qwen3-0.6b
text_cases.expected_dtype_note: expected_dtype_histogram is the count of tensors stored in the checkpoint file per safetensors dtype token (read from the header). The file stores 311 BF16 tensors; lm_head.weight is NOT stored (tie_word_embeddings=true, tied to embed_tokens). After loading, Python folds the tied head into the embedding (310 parameter arrays) while Java names the tied head as an extra lmHead.weight (311); both runtimes read the same 311 stored BF16 tensors and compute in BF16, so the matmuls are TF32-immune.
text_cases.identity_evidence: Qualification (both TF32 modes): per-step argmax and 16-step greedy match exactly across runtimes with max absolute logit diff 0.0; greedy-region minimum top-2 gap 0.5 is far above the 0.05 bound. The three gap-0 steps lie in the fixed-continuation region and are tie-eligible there.

text_cases.name: tinymistral-6x248m
text_cases.expected_dtype_note: The file stores 303 F32 tensors (all float32; not tied, so both lm_head and embed_tokens are stored). Both runtimes load the identical F32 tensors and compute in float32, so this case is TF32-sensitive. jmlx mixtral family: 12 layers, 6 experts, top-2 routing (Moe(6,2)), top-k float32 softmax in MoeMlp. Label all results as this smaller real MoE, not Mixtral-8x7B performance.
text_cases.identity_evidence: Qualification: per-step argmax and 16-step greedy match exactly across runtimes in both TF32 modes (max abs logit diff 5.30565e-3 at TF32=1, 1.52588e-5 at TF32=0); greedy-region minimum top-2 gap 0.116 >= 0.05 bound. Four below-bound steps (0.017-0.034) lie in the fixed-continuation region and are tie-eligible there.

text_cases.name: qwen3-8b-4bit
text_cases.expected_dtype_note: The file stores 907 tensors: 254 U32 (4-bit packed weights, including the U32-packed embed_tokens and lm_head) and 653 BF16 (scale/bias sidecars, norms, biases). Not tied. Both runtimes load the identical packed U32 layout with BF16 sidecars; effective compute is the artifact's 4-bit path with BF16 non-quantized leaves. No generation_config.json exists in the repository.
text_cases.identity_evidence: Qualification: per-step argmax and 16-step greedy match exactly across runtimes in both TF32 modes with max absolute logit diff 0.0, but two greedy-region steps are exact top-2 ties (gap 0.0 at greedy steps 6 and 10 of the 16-step run); the matched-greedy claim is therefore rejected for this case and the identity claim rests on the fixed continuation (31 of 33 steps hard-matched, 2 tie-eligible). Decode workload is per-token identical across runtimes, so timing remains comparable.
text_cases.page_cache_limitation: The 4.6 GB checkpoint is memory-mapped by the pinned MLX loader; for the 2048 prompt length the Java worker's 0.64 GiB float32 KV cache plus prefill activations evict the checkpoint page-cache pages during a run, so weight re-reads fall to SSD speed (~1.75 s per decode step vs ~13 ms compute-bound at 512). See the reference findings for the dd probe evidence and the WP1/WP2 mitigation decision.
